tasks.prompt: Sliplining a trunk reduces its diameter, and capacity complaints follow in wet weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario program evaluation. Before and after records cover the same reaches and seasons unless stated.

evidence.label: The sliplined trunk diameter fell from 900 mm to 800 mm, with a smoother pipe wall than the old rough concrete.
Dry weather flow passes with no change in depth.
In moderate storms the trunk now surcharges, which it did not do before lining at the same flows.
Upstream and downstream unlined sections do not surcharge at the same times.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The smoother wall fully offsets the smaller diameter at all flows
At high flows the diameter loss governs and capacity has fallen, even though dry flow is unaffected
The surcharge is caused by new development upstream
The downstream sections are causing the trunk surcharge

inference.explanation: Dry flow is unchanged, so the liner is not blocked, and the unlined sections stay free while the lined trunk surcharges at flows it used to pass. At high flow the reduced area governs despite the smoother wall. That is a capacity loss created by the rehabilitation choice.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Depth records in the lined trunk and the unlined sections during the same storms, at measured flows
Liner smoothness test certificates
Development application lists upstream

nextClue.explanation: Simultaneous depths at known flows show whether the lined section is the hydraulic bottleneck.

clueText.nc-a: Depths back up only in and above the lined trunk while downstream stays free, confirming the lined section limits capacity.
clueText.nc-b: Smoothness certificates do not measure capacity at storm flows.
clueText.nc-c: No flow increase from development is shown in the dry weather records.

tasks.prompt: A duplex station shows rising run hours on both pumps with no growth in its catchment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Total daily run hours for both pumps rose 40 percent over one year.
Drawdown tests show each pump now delivers 30 percent less flow than its commissioning test.
Wet well inflow measured during a dry week is unchanged from the prior year.
Both impellers show heavy wear and enlarged clearances on inspection.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Catchment inflow grew and the pumps are keeping up normally
Both pumps have lost capacity from impeller wear, so they run longer to move the same inflow
The level controls are calling for longer runs with healthy pumps
The run hour meters are both faulty in the same way

inference.explanation: Inflow is measured unchanged, both pumps test low by the same kind of margin, and both impellers show wear. Longer runs are the arithmetic result of moving the same volume at lower rate. Control or meter faults would not match failed drawdown tests and worn impellers on both units.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Drawdown test results at commissioning and now, with impeller clearance measurements
Catchment development records
Run hour meter purchase records

nextClue.explanation: Paired drawdown tests with clearance measurements directly confirm capacity loss and its mechanical cause.

clueText.nc-a: Current drawdown confirms the 30 percent loss and clearances are well beyond the commissioning values on both pumps.
clueText.nc-b: Development records show no catchment growth that could raise inflow.
clueText.nc-c: Meter records do not explain failed drawdown tests.

tasks.prompt: A station meets dry weather demand but surcharges its wet well in moderate rain, even after pump renewal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Both renewed pumps pass drawdown tests at their rated capacity.
Wet well level still rises to the high alarm in a 20 mm storm.
Upstream flow monitoring shows storm inflow peaks at three times the combined pump capacity for about one hour.
A neighbouring station with a larger wet well rides out the same storms without alarms.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The renewed pumps are still undersized in dry weather terms
The problem is peak inflow exceeding capacity plus too little wet well storage to shave the one hour peak
The high level alarm is set incorrectly
The upstream sewers are blocked and holding flow back

inference.explanation: Pumps test at rating, so the machinery is sound. The measured storm peak is three times combined capacity for about an hour, which no pump pair of that rating can pass in real time. Storage is what bridges such a peak, and the neighbour with more storage rides out the same storms.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Storm inflow hydrograph with wet well level and pump status for the same events
Pump nameplate photographs
Alarm setpoint list alone

nextClue.explanation: The combined hydrograph and level record shows whether inflow, capacity, or storage is the binding limit during the peak.

clueText.nc-a: Inflow exceeds combined capacity for about an hour and the level rise matches the unfilled storage volume.
clueText.nc-b: Nameplates state ratings, which the drawdown tests already confirmed.
clueText.nc-c: Setpoints do not change the measured inflow peak.

tasks.prompt: One pump in a triplex station trips on high temperature while the other two run normally.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: The tripping pump draws current 25 percent above nameplate before each trip.
Its discharge valve is found three quarters closed by a failed actuator that reports fully open.
The other two pumps discharge through their own fully open valves and draw normal current.
Cooling and ventilation in the station are normal and shared by all three pumps.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The station ventilation is overheating all motors
The tripping pump motor is failing internally
The partly closed discharge valve is forcing the pump to work against high head, raising current and temperature
The temperature sensor on that pump is faulty

inference.explanation: Only one pump is affected, it shares ventilation with healthy pumps, and it draws high current, which a faulty sensor would not cause. The partly closed valve with a false open signal gives a direct mechanical cause for high head, high current, and heating.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Valve actuator position check against actual stem position, with pump current during a test run
Ventilation maintenance records
Motor insulation test results alone

nextClue.explanation: Comparing indicated and actual valve position during a test run ties the high current to the restriction.

clueText.nc-a: The stem sits three quarters closed while the panel shows open, and current falls to normal when the valve is opened manually.
clueText.nc-b: Ventilation is shared and the other pumps run cool, so it cannot single out one pump.
clueText.nc-c: Insulation tests do not explain high running current that responds to valve position.

tasks.prompt: A station alternation failure is found after the standby pump seizes during a storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Panel records show the lead pump ran 98 percent of cycles for six months.
The alternator relay is found failed in one position.
The standby pump, called during a storm, is seized from long disuse and corrosion at its seal faces.
The lead pump shows wear consistent with double its expected duty.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The standby pump seized because of the storm inflow itself
Failed alternation concentrated all duty on one pump and left the standby to deteriorate unused, removing redundancy before the storm
Both pumps were equally worn and the seizure was chance
The storm inflow exceeded station capacity, which is the whole explanation

inference.explanation: Records prove one pump did nearly all the work for six months because the alternator failed, and the unused pump seized from disuse. The storm only revealed the lost redundancy. Equal wear and chance are contradicted by the run distribution and the relay finding.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Alternator relay test and the six month lead and lag run distribution from the panel log
Storm rainfall records
Pump purchase dates

nextClue.explanation: The relay test with the run distribution proves the alternation failure that produced both the overworn lead and the seized standby.

clueText.nc-a: The relay fails to switch on test and the log confirms one pump led 98 percent of cycles.
clueText.nc-b: Rainfall explains the demand that day, not six months of one sided running.
clueText.nc-c: Purchase dates do not show how duty was shared.

tasks.prompt: Wet well grease is blamed for pump failures, but the failure pattern points elsewhere.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Pumps fail by ragging at the suction, with wipes and fibrous material wound on the impellers.
Grease in the well is light and removed on the normal cleaning cycle.
The upstream catchment has no bar screen or grinder at the station inlet.
A sister station with a inlet screen in a similar catchment has no ragging failures.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Grease is the main cause of the impeller failures
Unscreened wipes and fibrous debris are ragging the pumps, and the comparison station shows screening prevents it
The pumps are too small for the catchment
Cleaning frequency for grease should be doubled to stop ragging

inference.explanation: The failed impellers carry wipes and fibre, not grease, and grease levels are light on a normal cycle. The screened sister station in a similar catchment has no such failures. More grease cleaning would not remove the wipes that are winding onto the impellers.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Impeller inspection photographs with the material removed, and the sister station failure history
Grease cleaning invoices
Pump sizing calculations

nextClue.explanation: The material on the impellers plus the screened station comparison identifies both the cause and a proven control.

clueText.nc-a: Photographs show wipes and fibre as the wrapping material, and the screened station records zero ragging failures in three years.
clueText.nc-b: Invoices show grease work was done, not what is wrapping the impellers.
clueText.nc-c: Sizing does not explain fibrous material wound on the impellers.

tasks.prompt: A station energy bill rises sharply while pumped volume stays the same.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Monthly energy use rose 35 percent over six months at constant pumped volume.
Discharge pressure at the same flow has risen steadily over the same period.
The force main air release valve at the high point is found seized and air bound on inspection.
Pump motors and drives test at normal efficiency.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pumps have become electrically inefficient
Air binding at the force main high point is raising the head the pumps must work against, increasing energy per volume
The utility raised its rates, which explains the higher energy use in kilowatt hours
Pumped volume records are under reporting the true volume

inference.explanation: Energy is measured in kilowatt hours, so a rate change cannot explain it. Motors test normal, while discharge pressure climbs and a seized air valve with air binding is found at the high point. Extra head at the same flow is extra energy per volume, which matches the bill.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Discharge pressure trend at constant flow, with the air valve inspection and a venting trial result
Utility rate schedules
Motor nameplate data

nextClue.explanation: A venting trial that drops pressure and energy at the same flow directly tests the air binding explanation.

clueText.nc-a: After manual venting, discharge pressure and energy per volume fall back near the earlier values.
clueText.nc-b: Rate schedules change cost, not kilowatt hours consumed.
clueText.nc-c: Nameplates state design efficiency, not the rising system head.

tasks.prompt: High level alarms cluster on weekend mornings at a station serving a growing suburb.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Alarms occur between 7 and 10 in the morning on weekends, with no rain.
Flow records show weekend morning inflow peaks 50 percent higher than weekday peaks.
Both pumps test at rated capacity and start correctly on every alarm.
Weekday peaks of the design year are matched, but the suburb has added homes since design.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pumps are failing on weekends
Weekend diurnal peaks from the grown catchment now exceed the original design peak the station was sized for
Rain is entering the system on weekends only
The alarm system generates false weekend alarms

inference.explanation: Pumps test and start correctly, alarms are dry weather, and measured weekend peaks exceed weekday peaks by half in a catchment that has grown past its design year. The station is being outgrown at its sharpest diurnal peak, not failing mechanically.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Diurnal flow curves for weekdays and weekends, with home counts at design and now
Alarm panel fault codes
Rainfall records for the alarm weekends

nextClue.explanation: Diurnal curves with growth counts show whether demand, not equipment, has crossed the design limit.

clueText.nc-a: Weekend peaks now exceed the design peak while weekday peaks sit at it, and home counts are 30 percent above design.
clueText.nc-b: No fault codes accompany the alarms, and the pumps start every time.
clueText.nc-c: The alarm weekends were dry, ruling out rain entry.

tasks.prompt: A station check valve failure is suspected from night cycling, and a test is designed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: At night with near zero inflow, the duty pump runs 14 short cycles per hour.
Wet well level falls during each run and rises quickly when the pump stops, at a rate far above measured inflow.
Daytime cycles at real inflow are normal in length.
The discharge header pressure holds steady between cycles.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Night inflow is much higher than believed
Pumped sewage is returning through a leaking check valve after each stop, refilling the well with the same water
The level floats are set too close together
The pump is oversized for night duty

inference.explanation: The well refills far faster than measured inflow only when the pump stops, which is the signature of flow returning from the force main through a leaking check valve. Close float settings would not make the level rise faster than inflow, and an oversized pump would still leave the well low between cycles.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: A closed valve isolation test, holding the well after a pump stop with the discharge valve shut and then open
Float setting measurements alone
Night water use estimates for the catchment

nextClue.explanation: The isolation test separates return flow from inflow, because shutting the discharge path should stop the fast refill if the check valve leaks.

clueText.nc-a: With the discharge valve shut the level holds steady, and reopening it restarts the fast refill, confirming return flow.
clueText.nc-b: Float settings affect cycle length, not a refill rate above inflow.
clueText.nc-c: Estimates cannot beat the measured near zero night inflow.

tasks.prompt: Pump run times lengthen after a force main cleaning, which surprises the crew.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Before cleaning, discharge pressure was high and pumps ran short, frequent cycles against a partly blocked main.
After pigging, discharge pressure fell to normal and flow per pump rose 45 percent.
Cycles are now longer but far fewer, and total daily run hours fell 20 percent.
Wet well inflow is unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cleaning damaged the force main and the pumps are losing flow
The pumps now move more water per run at normal pressure, so fewer, longer cycles move the same inflow with less total run time
The level controls were changed during the cleaning visit
Inflow fell at the same time by chance

inference.explanation: Pressure normalised, flow per pump rose, total run hours fell, and inflow is unchanged. Longer individual cycles with fewer starts is exactly what higher pump output looks like against the same inflow. Damage would raise pressure or run hours, and neither happened.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Before and after drawdown tests with cycle counts and total run hours at the same inflow
Pigging contractor invoice
Control panel setting printouts alone

nextClue.explanation: Paired drawdown and cycle records show output per run and total effort before and after, which settles whether the station improved.

clueText.nc-a: Drawdown confirms the 45 percent output rise and total run hours fell, matching the fewer and longer cycles.
clueText.nc-b: An invoice proves cleaning occurred, not its hydraulic effect.
clueText.nc-c: Settings were not changed, and printouts alone cannot explain the pressure fall.

tasks.prompt: A station floods its dry pit during testing of a newly installed larger pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station records. Run hours, levels and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: The new pump delivers 60 percent more flow than the unit it replaced.
During the test, a discharge flange joint in the dry pit weeps, then sprays under full flow pressure.
The flange bolts and gasket are the originals, reused from the smaller pump installation.
The wet well and suction side perform normally throughout.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The wet well is too small for the new pump
The reused discharge joint was not rated or renewed for the higher pressure and flow of the larger pump, and it failed under test
The suction line is blocked and causing the spray
The test was run too long and overheated the joint

inference.explanation: The spray is on the discharge side under full flow pressure, the suction side is normal, and the joint hardware was reused from a smaller duty. Higher discharge pressure on an unrenewed joint explains a weep growing to a spray. Wet well size cannot pressurise a dry pit flange.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Flange and gasket rating records for the joint, with pressure readings during a staged retest after renewal
Wet well dimension drawings
Suction pressure readings alone

nextClue.explanation: Ratings plus a staged retest after renewing the joint test whether the joint, not the station layout, was the weak point.

clueText.nc-a: The reused gasket rating is below the new pump shutoff pressure, and the renewed joint holds through a full staged retest.
clueText.nc-b: Well dimensions do not pressurise discharge piping.
clueText.nc-c: Suction readings were normal and cannot explain a discharge spray.

tasks.prompt: Force main pressure rises slowly over two years while station flow falls.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Discharge pressure at the same pump flow has risen 18 percent in two years.
Pigging returns contain heavy black scale and tuberculation debris.
After pigging, pressure drops most of the way back toward the original value, then climbs again over months.
Pump drawdown tests at the station are unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pumps are wearing out and producing more pressure
Internal scale and tuberculation are narrowing the main, and pigging temporarily restores the bore
The discharge pressure gauge is drifting upward
A partly closed valve at the discharge manhole explains everything, including the pigging debris

inference.explanation: Pumps test unchanged, pigging returns are full of scale, and pressure resets after pigging then climbs again. That cycle fits progressive internal narrowing. A gauge drift would not produce debris or respond to pigging, and a valve would not fill pigs with scale.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Pressure trend at constant flow across a pigging event, with pig return debris records
Pressure gauge calibration certificate alone
Valve position records at the discharge manhole

nextClue.explanation: The pressure response to pigging, paired with what the pigs bring back, directly tests internal narrowing.

clueText.nc-a: Pressure falls sharply after pigging and climbs again over months, and returns carry scale matching the pipe material.
clueText.nc-b: A certificate does not explain debris or the pigging response.
clueText.nc-c: The discharge valve is confirmed open and unchanged through the period.

tasks.prompt: A force main air release program is judged by pressure and energy results.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Before the program, two high point air valves were seized and discharge pressure was 12 percent above design.
After valve renewal and scheduled exercising, discharge pressure returned to design at the same flows.
Energy per megalitre pumped fell 10 percent.
No pump or main changes were made during the program.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pressure fall came from pump improvements made at the same time
Restoring air release at the high points removed air binding and returned the main to design head, cutting energy
Flows fell during the program, which explains both changes
Air valves have no effect on force main pressure

inference.explanation: Nothing else changed, flows are stated the same, and both pressure and energy returned to design values after the air valves were restored. Air pockets at high points reduce bore and add head, so removing them explains both results together.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Before and after pressure and energy at matched flows, with the valve condition records
Pump maintenance invoices for the period
Annual energy totals without flows

nextClue.explanation: Matched flow comparisons isolate the air program effect from flow or pump changes.

clueText.nc-a: At matched flows pressure and energy both sit at design values after the program, and the seized valves are documented before it.
clueText.nc-b: No pump work invoices exist for the period.
clueText.nc-c: Totals without flows cannot show energy per volume.

tasks.prompt: A force main bursts repeatedly at the same low point after pump starts.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Three bursts in two years occur at the same low point fitting within days of pump restarts after maintenance.
Pressure logging shows sharp transient spikes at pump start, highest at the low point.
Steady running pressure at the low point is within the pipe rating.
The air valve at the upstream high point is seized shut.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Steady pressure is slowly fatiguing the pipe at its weakest fitting
Start up transients, worsened by a seized air valve that cannot cushion or admit air, are spiking pressure at the low point beyond steady values
The fitting material is defective throughout the whole main
External corrosion at the low point is the sole cause

inference.explanation: Bursts follow restarts, steady pressure is within rating, and logging shows start up spikes peaking at the low point. A seized high point air valve removes the cushion that limits such transients. A whole main material defect would not cluster at one fitting after restarts.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Transient pressure traces at the low point during controlled starts, before and after air valve renewal
Steady pressure records alone
Soil corrosivity survey for the route

nextClue.explanation: Transient traces across the air valve renewal test whether the spikes, and their control, match the burst pattern.

clueText.nc-a: Spikes exceed the fitting rating before renewal and fall well below it after the air valve is restored.
clueText.nc-b: Steady records are within rating and cannot explain bursts timed to restarts.
clueText.nc-c: Soil survey does not explain the restart timing.

tasks.prompt: Sewage arrives septic from a force main serving a small community with long detention.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Force main detention time at average flow is about 14 hours.
Discharged sewage is black with strong sulfide odour, worst on Monday mornings after low weekend flows.
Hydrogen sulfide at the discharge manhole corrodes the concrete crown.
A shorter force main in the same town discharges fresh sewage with no odour.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The community produces unusually strong sewage at the treatment end
Long detention in the force main lets sewage go septic and generate sulfide, which is released and corrodes at the discharge
The discharge manhole ventilation is the root cause of the septicity
Weekend water use changes the sewage strength enough to explain the pattern

inference.explanation: Detention of 14 hours, worse after low flow weekends, black septic discharge, and crown corrosion at the release point all fit sulfide generation inside the main. The short main discharging fresh sewage in the same town rules out a community wide sewage strength cause. Ventilation affects release, not generation.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Detention time calculation at weekday and weekend flows, with sulfide readings at the discharge across a week
Treatment plant influent strength records
Manhole ventilation fan specifications

nextClue.explanation: Sulfide tracked against detention time tests whether time in the main, longest on weekends, drives the septicity.

clueText.nc-a: Sulfide peaks after the longest detention periods and is lowest after high flow weekdays, matching the generation pattern.
clueText.nc-b: Plant influent mixes many sources and cannot isolate this main.
clueText.nc-c: Fan size affects odour release at the manhole, not sulfide formed in the main.

tasks.prompt: Two stations share a force main, and a capacity study separates their interaction.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Each station alone pumps at its rated flow into the shared main.
When both run together, each delivers about 30 percent less and pressures rise at both.
The shared section is the original size, sized for one station when built.
Check valves at both stations test as holding, with no return flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both pumps have worn at the same rate
The shared section is the bottleneck, because combined flow raises friction head beyond what either pump pair can sustain at rating
The check valves leak only when both stations run
The wet wells are too small when both stations run

inference.explanation: Each station performs alone, valves hold, and the penalty appears only in combined running through a section sized for one station. That is shared friction head, not pump wear, which would also appear in solo running.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Flow and pressure at both stations in solo and combined running at the same wet well levels
Pump wear inspection reports
Wet well dimension drawings

nextClue.explanation: Solo versus combined tests at matched levels isolate the shared main as the only changed condition.

clueText.nc-a: Solo runs meet rating at both stations, and combined runs lose the same share at both, with the pressure rise located in the shared section.
clueText.nc-b: Inspections show pumps within wear limits.
clueText.nc-c: Well size does not change friction in the shared main.

tasks.prompt: A force main leak is localised by pressure decay testing between isolation valves.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Station flow is normal but pressure along the main falls faster than the design profile.
Isolated section tests show one 300 m section loses pressure overnight while the others hold.
A wet area with sewage odour sits above that section, which crosses a farm field.
Pump and station piping tests are normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pumps are losing prime and causing the pressure profile change
The pressure losing section contains a leak, confirmed by the surface evidence above it
All sections leak equally and the test is misleading
The wet area is a natural spring unrelated to the main

inference.explanation: Only one isolated section loses pressure while others hold, station equipment tests normal, and the wet odorous area sits directly above that section. That combination localises a leak to that section. Equal leakage is contradicted by the holding sections.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Section by section pressure hold results with a surface survey of the losing section
Pump priming records
Design pressure profile drawings alone

nextClue.explanation: Hold results by section plus the surface survey pinpoint the leaking length for excavation.

clueText.nc-a: Only the field section fails the hold test and excavation there finds a cracked joint at the wet area.
clueText.nc-b: Priming records are normal and do not explain a single section loss.
clueText.nc-c: Drawings show design, not the as found pressure loss.

tasks.prompt: Force main velocity is too low at night and solids deposition is confirmed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Night flow velocity in the main is about 0.4 m/s for six hours.
Pigs return loaded with grit and settled solids after every run.
Morning pump starts show a pressure surge that clears within minutes, consistent with moving a solids bed.
Daytime velocity reaches 1.1 m/s and pressures are normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The main is oversized for current flows, so night velocities let solids settle that morning flows then disturb
The pigs are picking up material from the station wet well, not the main
The pressure surge is a water hammer defect in the pumps
Grit in the returns comes from a construction site upstream

inference.explanation: Low night velocity, grit loaded pigs from the main itself, and a morning surge that clears as the bed moves all fit deposition during slow hours in an oversized main. Daytime normality rules out a standing pump defect, and pigs travel the main, not the wet well.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Velocity profile across a full day, with pig return volumes trended against night flow
Wet well cleaning records
Construction site inspection reports

nextClue.explanation: Matching deposition evidence to the hours when velocity falls below self cleansing values tests the oversizing explanation.

clueText.nc-a: Pig returns are heaviest after the longest low velocity nights and lightest after high flow days.
clueText.nc-b: Wet well records do not explain material collected along the main length.
clueText.nc-c: No construction discharge to this catchment is recorded.

tasks.prompt: A cathodic and coating assessment finds force main wall loss concentrated at air pockets.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Ultrasonic thickness readings show the greatest wall loss at the crown near high points of the steel main.
Low points and invert readings are near original thickness.
Air valves on the route were neglected for years and two were seized.
Internal inspection shows corrosion tubercles at the crown and clean metal at the invert.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The invert should show the worst loss because solids scour it
Trapped air at high points creates an air and sewage interface that drives crown corrosion, worsened by failed air valves
External soil corrosion explains the internal crown pattern
The thickness gauge reads low wherever the pipe curves upward

inference.explanation: Loss is internal, at the crown, at high points, with seized air valves, while the invert stays sound. That is the air pocket interface pattern. Soil corrosion would attack the outside, and scour would mark the invert, the opposite of what is measured.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Thickness map by clock position and chainage, with air valve service history
Soil corrosivity results alone
Gauge calibration certificate alone

nextClue.explanation: A thickness map against valve history shows whether loss follows the air pocket locations.

clueText.nc-a: Wall loss peaks at the crown within metres of each neglected high point and is minimal elsewhere.
clueText.nc-b: Soil results cannot produce an internal crown only pattern.
clueText.nc-c: Calibration does not explain a pattern that follows high points.

tasks.prompt: After a force main repair, station flow stays low and pressure stays high.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: An emergency repair replaced a burst section, and from that day flow fell and pressure rose in one step.
The repair used a temporary smaller diameter spool piece, still in place a year later.
Pump tests at the station meet rating into a test header.
Pressure readings show the largest single drop occurs across the repaired section.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both pumps were damaged by the burst
The undersized temporary spool is a permanent bottleneck creating the step change in flow and pressure
The main has scaled up along its whole length in one day
Air entered during the repair and has stayed trapped for a year

inference.explanation: The change is a step on the repair day, pumps test fine, and the pressure drop concentrates across the repaired section with its smaller spool. Whole main scaling does not happen in a day, and trapped air would not localise the pressure drop at the spool for a year.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Pressure profile along the main at a known flow, before and after spool replacement
Pump test certificates alone
Pigging records for the whole main

nextClue.explanation: A pressure profile at known flow locates the loss, and retesting after spool renewal confirms it.

clueText.nc-a: The profile shows most of the loss across the 6 m spool, and replacing it with full size pipe restores original flow and pressure.
clueText.nc-b: Pump tests are already normal and cannot locate a main restriction.
clueText.nc-c: Pigging the whole main treats scaling that the step timing already rules out.

tasks.prompt: A force main detention study guides a sulfide control choice at the discharge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main records. Pressures, flows and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Detention ranges from 4 hours at peak flow to 16 hours overnight.
Sulfide at the discharge tracks detention, highest after overnight low flows.
Corrosion is severe in the first two manholes below the discharge and mild beyond them.
A trial that raised night pumping frequency, shortening detention, cut morning sulfide by half.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Corrosion below the discharge is caused by road salt runoff
Sulfide generated during long detention is released at the discharge and attacks the first manholes, so detention control is a valid lever
The manholes were built with defective concrete only in the first two structures
Sulfide forms in the manholes themselves, not in the main

inference.explanation: Sulfide tracks time in the main, the trial that shortened detention cut sulfide, and corrosion fades with distance below the release point as sulfide disperses. Defective concrete in exactly the first two manholes and road salt do not explain the detention link or the trial result.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide and corrosion survey before and after a sustained detention reduction schedule
Concrete delivery records for the manholes
Road salt application records

nextClue.explanation: A sustained schedule change with repeat surveys shows whether detention control holds sulfide and corrosion down.

clueText.nc-a: Morning sulfide stays near the trial values under the new schedule and corrosion rates in the first manholes slow.
clueText.nc-b: Delivery records cannot explain sulfide that responds to pumping schedules.
clueText.nc-c: Salt records do not track overnight detention patterns.

tasks.prompt: Odour complaints map tightly around one drop manhole, and the pattern is analysed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: Complaints come from homes within 60 m of a manhole where a sewer drops 3 m.
Complaints peak on warm mornings after low flow nights.
Sulfide readings in the manhole air reach their daily high at the same morning hours.
Manholes upstream and downstream on the same sewer draw no complaints.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The whole sewer is septic and odour escapes everywhere equally
Turbulence at the drop strips sulfide from slow, septic overnight sewage into the manhole air, localising odour at that structure
A nearby restaurant is the odour source
Residents complain in the morning because they are home then, with no real odour peak

inference.explanation: Complaints, sulfide readings, and timing all peak together at one structure with a 3 m drop, after low flow nights that let sewage turn septic. Neighbouring manholes on the same sewer are quiet, which rules out a whole sewer or neighbourhood source.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide logging in the drop manhole and its neighbours across several days, with complaint times
Restaurant inspection records
A resident survey on daily routines

nextClue.explanation: Simultaneous logging at the drop and its neighbours tests whether the drop structure itself creates the peak.

clueText.nc-a: Sulfide spikes only at the drop manhole in the morning hours and matches complaint times, while neighbours stay low.
clueText.nc-b: No restaurant discharge fault is found, and odour peaks track sulfide, not kitchen hours.
clueText.nc-c: Routines do not explain measured sulfide spikes at one structure.

tasks.prompt: Corrosion is severe in a gravity sewer downstream of a long flat reach, and mild in a steep reach.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: The flat reach runs slow and deep, with sewage detention of several hours in warm weather.
Its downstream manholes show crown corrosion and soft concrete above the flow line.
The steep reach runs fast and shallow with the same sewage sources, and its manholes are sound.
Sulfide readings are high leaving the flat reach and low leaving the steep reach.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Concrete quality differs between the two reaches
Slow warm detention in the flat reach generates sulfide that corrodes crowns downstream, while fast flow in the steep reach limits generation
The flat reach receives industrial acid discharges
Crown corrosion is caused by condensation alone in both reaches

inference.explanation: Same sources, different hydraulics. High sulfide leaves the flat reach and corrosion follows it, while the steep reach stays low in sulfide and sound. Condensation alone would affect both reaches, and no acid discharge is reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide and detention comparison for both reaches in the same warm period, with crown condition surveys
Concrete delivery records by reach
Industrial discharge permits for the catchment

nextClue.explanation: Paired sulfide, detention, and condition data test whether generation in the flat reach drives the downstream corrosion.

clueText.nc-a: Sulfide rises along the flat reach with detention time and crowns below it are corroded, while the steep reach shows neither.
clueText.nc-b: Concrete records show the same supplier and mix for both reaches.
clueText.nc-c: No acid discharge permits or events are recorded.

tasks.prompt: A chemical dosing trial at a lift station is evaluated for odour control downstream.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: Before dosing, sulfide at the force main discharge averaged high on summer mornings.
During dosing, discharge sulfide fell by 70 percent and complaints stopped.
Two weeks after dosing ended, sulfide and complaints returned to pre trial values.
Flows and temperatures were similar across all three periods.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The trial coincided with cooler weather that cut sulfide naturally
The dosing caused the reduction, because sulfide fell during dosing and returned when dosing stopped under similar conditions
Complaints stopped because residents left on holiday
The sulfide meter drifted during the trial month

inference.explanation: The on and off pattern under similar flow and temperature is the classic test of cause. Sulfide fell only while dosing ran and returned when it stopped. Weather, holidays, and drift do not explain a return to the same baseline after the trial.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide trend across the before, during, and after periods with dosing records and temperatures
Resident holiday survey
Meter purchase records

nextClue.explanation: The three period trend with dosing records is the evidence that separates a dosing effect from background variation.

clueText.nc-a: Sulfide steps down at dosing start and steps back up at dosing stop, with temperatures flat across the steps.
clueText.nc-b: No survey explains measured sulfide steps at the discharge.
clueText.nc-c: Purchase records do not show field drift, and the meter returned to baseline values after the trial.

tasks.prompt: Odour at a subdivision appears two years after homes connect to a long trunk, and grows each summer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: The trunk detention at current flows is about 9 hours, up from 5 hours before the subdivision connected, because added flow is offset by a long flat profile.
Complaints are strongest in the first summer after connection and stronger each hotter summer.
Sulfide at the subdivision outlet manhole is high in summer and low in winter.
The subdivision internal sewers are steep, clean, and complaint free at their upper ends.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The subdivision internal sewers are generating the odour at their upper ends
Long trunk detention generates sulfide that is released at the outlet manhole, with generation rising in warm weather
Home plumbing traps are drying out across the subdivision
A new food plant in the subdivision is discharging sulfide directly

inference.explanation: Upper internal sewers are clean and complaint free, while sulfide at the outlet is seasonal and detention nearly doubled after connection. That points to generation during long warm detention in the trunk, released where flow exits. Trap drying would scatter complaints by home, not concentrate them at the outlet.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide logging at the outlet manhole across seasons, with trunk detention estimates
Home plumbing inspection sample results
Food plant discharge records

nextClue.explanation: Seasonal sulfide at the outlet against detention tests the trunk generation explanation directly.

clueText.nc-a: Outlet sulfide tracks temperature and detention, peaking in hot spells and falling in winter, while home inspections find traps full.
clueText.nc-b: Home inspections contradict the dry trap idea.
clueText.nc-c: No food plant discharge of sulfide is recorded.

tasks.prompt: A manhole rehabilitation coating fails early at one structure but holds at others.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: Coated manholes in moderate sulfide areas hold after three years.
The failed structure sits directly below a force main discharge with the highest sulfide readings in the system.
Its coating shows blistering and loss at the crown within one year.
Surface preparation records for the failed structure show coating applied over damp, unsound concrete to save time.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The coating product is defective everywhere
Severe sulfide exposure plus poor surface preparation at that one structure explain the early failure, while prepared structures in milder exposure hold
The failed structure was coated by a different product batch by chance
Groundwater pressure behind the coating is the sole cause everywhere

inference.explanation: The same product holds where preparation was proper and exposure milder. The failed structure combines the worst exposure with documented damp, unsound substrate. Product wide failure is contradicted by the holding structures.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Coating inspection results by structure, paired with preparation records and sulfide exposure class
Product marketing data sheets
Coating invoice totals

nextClue.explanation: Pairing condition with preparation and exposure shows whether failure follows the documented shortcut and severity, not the product alone.

clueText.nc-a: Every early failure sits on a structure with a preparation shortcut, and all properly prepared structures hold, including one in high exposure.
clueText.nc-b: Data sheets describe the product, not the as applied condition.
clueText.nc-c: Invoices do not record substrate condition.

tasks.prompt: Ventilation changes at a wet well reduce worker sulfide readings but odour complaints outside continue.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: After ventilation upgrades, sulfide readings inside the wet well during entries fall to low values.
Odour complaints from nearby homes continue at the same rate, peaking after pump runs.
The vent stack discharges untreated air at roof height near the homes.
Sulfide generation in the incoming sewage is unchanged by the ventilation.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Ventilation has eliminated the sulfide problem entirely
Ventilation protects workers inside but moves the same sulfide load out the stack, so outside odour needs source or treatment control, not more air changes
Complaints continue because residents dislike the station building
The pumps generate sulfide when they run

inference.explanation: Inside readings fell, which is a worker protection success, but generation is unchanged and the stack discharges untreated air near homes after pump runs stir the sewage. The load is relocated, not removed. Pumps do not generate sulfide, they release what detention formed.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Stack discharge sulfide readings during pump runs, with complaint timing and inside entry readings
Resident attitude survey
Pump motor inspection reports

nextClue.explanation: Stack readings during pump runs test whether the outside odour is the relocated load.

clueText.nc-a: Stack sulfide peaks during pump runs and matches complaint timing, while entry readings stay low.
clueText.nc-b: Attitudes do not produce measured stack sulfide peaks.
clueText.nc-c: Motor reports do not address sewage sulfide at all.

tasks.prompt: Corrosion rates double in a sewer after an upstream industry changes its discharge pattern.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: The industry now discharges warm wastewater in long batches, raising sewer temperature by 3 C for hours.
Sulfide readings downstream rose after the change, with no change in domestic sewage flow.
Crown corrosion surveys show the rate of concrete loss doubling in the two years after the change.
A parallel sewer without the industrial discharge shows unchanged sulfide and corrosion.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The concrete reached an age where corrosion naturally doubles
Warmer sewage speeds sulfide generation, and the parallel sewer control shows the change is tied to the industrial discharge pattern
Domestic growth explains the sulfide rise
The corrosion survey method changed and created the difference

inference.explanation: The change follows the discharge change in time, has a mechanism in warmer sewage generating sulfide faster, and is absent in the parallel control sewer. Domestic flow is unchanged, and the same survey method shows no change where the discharge is absent.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide and temperature trends before and after the change, in both sewers, with corrosion depth surveys
Concrete age records alone
Domestic connection counts

nextClue.explanation: The two sewer comparison across the change date separates the discharge effect from ageing or method effects.

clueText.nc-a: Only the receiving sewer shows warmer sewage, higher sulfide, and faster crown loss after the change.
clueText.nc-b: Age is the same story in the control sewer, where nothing changed.
clueText.nc-c: Domestic counts are flat in both catchments.

tasks.prompt: A biofilter at a station vent cuts complaints, then complaints return after a dry summer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: The biofilter cut stack odour sharply in its first year and complaints nearly stopped.
In the second summer, complaints return during a long dry spell.
Inspection finds the biofilter media dry and cracked, with air channelling through gaps.
The irrigation system for the media is found valved off after a winter repair.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The biofilter media is exhausted and must be replaced
Dry, cracked media with the irrigation left off lets air bypass treatment, so restoring moisture should restore performance
Sulfide generation doubled in the dry summer
Residents became more sensitive to the same odour level

inference.explanation: The media is physically dry and channelled with its water supply left off, which is a complete bypass mechanism. Generation records are not shown to change, and media that failed from dryness is not the same as exhausted media. Restoring irrigation is the testable fix.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Media moisture readings and stack odour before and after rewetting the bed
Media replacement quotations
Sulfide generation records at the station inlet

nextClue.explanation: Rewetting with before and after stack readings tests the bypass explanation before any media purchase.

clueText.nc-a: After irrigation is restored and the bed rewets, stack odour falls back to first year values within days.
clueText.nc-b: Quotations price a replacement that the rewetting result may make unnecessary.
clueText.nc-c: Inlet sulfide is steady across the dry spell, ruling out a generation doubling.

tasks.prompt: Sulfide corrosion is found in a sewer that receives a septage hauling discharge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: Septage is discharged at one manhole in large loads, three afternoons per week.
Sewage below that manhole tests high in sulfide on discharge afternoons and normal on other days.
Crown corrosion is severe for 200 m below the manhole and mild above it and beyond that length.
The hauler discharge records match the high sulfide afternoons exactly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sewer concrete is defective for exactly 200 m
Septage loads bring high strength, septic waste that raises sulfide locally, and corrosion follows the affected length
Domestic sewage on those afternoons is stronger by coincidence
The sulfide meter reads high whenever trucks are present

inference.explanation: Timing matches hauler records, corrosion starts at the discharge point and fades with distance, and the pipe above is mild. A 200 m concrete defect matching discharge days is not credible, and meter readings are backed by the physical corrosion pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sulfide sampling above and below the manhole on discharge and non discharge days
Concrete delivery records for the reach
Truck scheduling records alone

nextClue.explanation: Paired sampling on both day types isolates what the septage adds at that manhole.

clueText.nc-a: Sulfide below the manhole is several times higher on discharge afternoons and normal otherwise, while above stays normal on all days.
clueText.nc-b: Delivery records cannot explain day by day sulfide swings.
clueText.nc-c: Schedules alone show timing, sampling shows the actual load added.

tasks.prompt: An odour study must separate sewer odour from a nearby landfill source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour and corrosion investigation. Monitoring results are as stated.

evidence.label: Complaints peak when wind blows from the landfill toward the homes, regardless of sewer conditions.
Sewer sulfide readings at the nearest manholes are low on the worst complaint days.
Complaint odour is described as sweet and garbage like, not rotten egg.
On calm days with high sewer sulfide, complaints are few.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sewer is the main source and wind direction is a coincidence
The pattern fits the landfill as the main source for these complaints, because they track wind from the landfill and not sewer sulfide peaks
Both sources contribute equally on all days
Residents cannot describe odours reliably, so descriptions should be ignored

inference.explanation: Complaints follow wind from the landfill, occur when sewer sulfide is low, and carry a garbage description rather than rotten egg. High sewer sulfide on calm days draws few complaints. Every line points away from the sewer for this complaint set.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Complaint log plotted against wind direction and same day manhole sulfide readings
Landfill operating hours alone
Sewer cleaning records for the street

nextClue.explanation: Plotting complaints against both wind and sulfide at once shows which source the pattern actually follows.

clueText.nc-a: Complaints cluster on landfill wind days at all sulfide levels, and are rare on high sulfide calm days.
clueText.nc-b: Operating hours alone do not show transport to the homes.
clueText.nc-c: Cleaning records do not explain a wind direction pattern.

tasks.prompt: A FOG program reports success from fewer backups, and an analyst checks for other causes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: Backups in the program area fell 45 percent in the first program year.
In the same year, the city also jetted the program area sewers twice as often as before.
A matched area with the extra jetting but no FOG program saw backups fall 40 percent.
Grease found in jetting returns fell sharply in both areas.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The FOG program alone caused the 45 percent fall
The extra jetting explains most of the fall in both areas, so the program effect cannot be claimed from backup counts alone
Backups fell because restaurants closed across the city
Jetting has no effect on grease backups

inference.explanation: The comparison area with jetting alone achieved nearly the same reduction, and grease in returns fell in both. That means jetting is a competing explanation that backup counts alone cannot rule out. Program credit needs a measure jetting does not produce, such as interceptor compliance or discharge quality.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Interceptor inspection and compliance records for the program area, with backup trends in both areas
Program area backup counts alone
Restaurant closure lists

nextClue.explanation: Compliance records test the program mechanism directly, while the two area comparison shows how much jetting already explains.

clueText.nc-a: Compliance rose from 30 to 85 percent in the program area, giving the program a real mechanism, while jetting explains the shared backup fall.
clueText.nc-b: Counts alone repeat the confounded comparison.
clueText.nc-c: No unusual closures occurred in either area.

tasks.prompt: Interceptor inspections find most units undersized for the premises they serve.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: Inspected interceptors fill to their grease capacity in about one third of the required service interval.
Premises with the undersized units report the most frequent sewer grease findings downstream.
Correctly sized units on the same street hold to their service interval with room to spare.
Cleaning frequency is the same for both groups because the bylaw sets one interval.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cleaning crews are skipping the undersized units
Fixed interval cleaning cannot work for undersized units, because they reach capacity long before the interval ends and then pass grease
The premises with undersized units cook different food
Downstream grease comes from homes, not these premises

inference.explanation: Capacity is reached in a third of the interval, correctly sized neighbours on the same interval stay within capacity, and downstream grease tracks the undersized group. A single fixed interval cannot protect a unit that fills three times faster. Food type is not shown to differ.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Interceptor capacity and measured fill rate records, with downstream CCTV grease findings by premises
Cleaning crew timesheets
Home cooking surveys for the street

nextClue.explanation: Fill rate against capacity shows exactly which units outrun the fixed interval and pass grease.

clueText.nc-a: Every unit passing grease fills before mid interval, and every unit within capacity at service shows a clean downstream pipe.
clueText.nc-b: Timesheets show the units were serviced on schedule.
clueText.nc-c: Home surveys cannot explain grease that tracks specific premises laterals.

tasks.prompt: A FOG education campaign runs, and grease findings downstream do not change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: The campaign delivered leaflets and posters to all food premises in the district.
Interceptor inspection rates and service records did not change during the campaign year.
Downstream CCTV grease grades are the same before and after the campaign.
A neighbouring district that added inspections in the same year saw grease grades fall.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The campaign failed because leaflets were the wrong colour
Education without inspection or enforcement changed no behaviour that affects grease, while the district that added inspections improved
CCTV cannot measure grease change over a year
Grease grades were already at the lowest possible level

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Interceptor service and inspection records for both districts, with before and after CCTV grease grades
Leaflet distribution counts
Poster design files

nextClue.explanation: Service behaviour records are the mechanism test, because grease only falls when what premises do changes.

clueText.nc-b: Distribution counts show paper delivered, not behaviour changed.
clueText.nc-c: Design files say nothing about discharge behaviour.

tasks.prompt: Grease hot spots move downstream after a cleaning program change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: The city switched a hot spot reach from scraping and collection to high pressure jetting only.
The reach itself now passes CCTV as mostly clean.
The lift station 300 m downstream now fouls its floats with grease within days of each jetting visit.
Station fouling dates match jetting dates for the reach.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Jetting is mobilising grease from the reach and delivering it to the station, where it recoats the floats
Restaurant discharges increased on exactly the jetting days
Float fouling is an electrical fault pattern

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Jetting dates paired with station cleaning dates and grease volumes removed at the station
Station electrical test reports
Restaurant discharge permits

nextClue.explanation: Date pairing shows whether station grease arrives as a direct result of reach jetting.

clueText.nc-b: Electrical tests are normal and cannot deposit grease on floats.
clueText.nc-c: Permits do not change on jetting days.

tasks.prompt: A premises with a well maintained interceptor still shows grease in its lateral.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: The interceptor is correctly sized, serviced on schedule, and inspection shows it working with a clear outlet.
Grease is found in the lateral between the kitchen and the interceptor, coating the pipe before the unit.
Staff report pouring fryer oil into a sink that bypasses the interceptor and drains straight to the lateral.
Downstream of the interceptor, the sewer is clean.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

The bypass sink is sending oil straight to the lateral, so the grease never reaches the interceptor that is working correctly
The lateral grease migrates upstream from the sewer
The inspection method cannot judge an interceptor

inference.explanation: The unit works with a clear outlet and the sewer below it is clean, while grease sits before the unit and staff describe a bypass sink in daily use. Grease cannot migrate upstream from a clean sewer. The plumbing layout, not the interceptor, is the fault.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Plumbing layout check tracing each kitchen fixture to the interceptor or to the bypass
A second interceptor inspection a month later
Sewer CCTV below the premises alone

nextClue.explanation: Tracing fixtures shows which flows ever reach the interceptor, which is the deciding fact.

clueText.nc-a: Two sinks and the fryer drain bypass the interceptor entirely, and correcting the layout clears the lateral grease.
clueText.nc-b: A repeat inspection would again find a working unit and miss the bypass.
clueText.nc-c: The sewer below is already known clean.

tasks.prompt: FOG program data show backups falling only in streets where cleaning also changed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: Streets with FOG inspections plus scraping and collection show backup falls of 50 percent.
Streets with FOG inspections but unchanged jetting only cleaning show backup falls of 5 percent.
Interceptor compliance rose equally in both street groups.
Grease grades on CCTV fell sharply only in the scraping group.

The scraping streets had fewer restaurants to begin with
CCTV grease grades do not relate to backups

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Street by street compliance, cleaning method, CCTV grease grade and backup records
Program wide average backup change
Restaurant counts by street alone

nextClue.explanation: The street level pairing shows whether the same compliance produced different results under different cleaning, which the average hides.

clueText.nc-b: A program average blends the two opposite results into a misleading middle.
clueText.nc-c: Restaurant counts are similar across groups and do not track the split.

tasks.prompt: A bakery with no fryers is exempted from the FOG program, and grease appears below it.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: The bakery washes down large volumes of butter and shortening based mixes daily.
CCTV shows the pipe clean above the bakery lateral and greasy below it.
The bakery has no interceptor because its exemption assumed no frying means no grease.
Other premises on the street have interceptors and clean downstream pipes.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?
