Washdown of butter and shortening is a real grease load, so the fryer based exemption left a genuine source uncontrolled
The bakery grease is actually root material misidentified
The clean pipe above the bakery is the anomaly to investigate

inference.explanation: The pipe turns greasy exactly at the bakery lateral, the bakery discharges fatty washdown daily with no interceptor, and controlled premises nearby leave clean pipes. Frying is not the only grease source, washdown of fats is enough.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: CCTV above and below the bakery lateral, with a washdown observation at the bakery
Exemption policy wording alone
Root defect logs for the reach

nextClue.explanation: The above and below comparison plus the washdown observation ties the load to the exempted premises.

clueText.nc-a: Washdown runs milky with fat and the pipe below coats within weeks, while above stays clean.
clueText.nc-b: Policy wording states the assumption that the evidence contradicts.
clueText.nc-c: No roots are coded on this reach.

tasks.prompt: Interceptor service records look complete, but field checks find units untouched.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: Submitted service records claim every unit was pumped on schedule.
Field depth checks at a sample of units find grease and solids at levels needing months of accumulation.
Hauler disposal manifests show volumes far below what full pumping of all units would produce.
Downstream grease findings did not improve during the record period.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The field depth check method overstates accumulation
The paper records do not reflect work actually done, because manifests and field depths both show much less pumping than claimed
Interceptors fill faster than any service could match
Downstream grease is unrelated to interceptor service

inference.explanation: Two independent measures, field depths and disposal volumes, both contradict the submitted records, and downstream results show no improvement. Faster filling cannot explain manifest volumes below a single full pump out round.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Manifest volumes totalled against the summed capacity of units claimed serviced, with the field depth sample
Submitted service records reviewed again
Hauler vehicle maintenance records

nextClue.explanation: Manifest totals against claimed work is an arithmetic check that paper review alone cannot provide.

clueText.nc-a: Manifests total about one fifth of the volume that pumping all claimed units would produce, matching the field depths.
clueText.nc-b: Reviewing the same records again repeats the claim being tested.
clueText.nc-c: Vehicle records do not measure what was pumped from each unit.

tasks.prompt: A FOG bylaw takes effect and grease falls in one district but not another with the same bylaw.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: Both districts fall under the same new bylaw and received the same notices.
District 1 hired inspectors who visit premises and follow up on failed units.
District 2 relies on mailed notices with no visits or follow up.
After two years, District 1 grease grades and backups fell sharply, District 2 is unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The bylaw text works in one district by chance
Enforcement presence, not the bylaw text alone, produced the improvement, because the visited district changed and the mailed only district did not
District 2 restaurants cook with less grease, hiding the bylaw effect
District 1 improvement came from its newer sewers

inference.explanation: The bylaw and notices are identical, so the difference is the follow up model. The visited district improved and the unvisited did not. Sewer age and cooking differences are not reported, and chance does not explain a two year district wide split aligned with enforcement.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Premises visit and follow up records by district, with grease grade trends
The bylaw text
Sewer age maps alone

nextClue.explanation: Visit records against grease trends test whether contact, rather than paper, drove the change.

clueText.nc-a: Premises with visits corrected their units at high rates, unvisited premises rarely did, and grease followed the same split.
clueText.nc-b: The text is the same for both districts and cannot explain different outcomes.
clueText.nc-c: Age maps do not track which premises corrected their units.

tasks.prompt: Seasonal grease peaks follow a festival calendar in a tourist district.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats, oils and grease program records. Inspection and cleaning results are as stated.

evidence.label: Grease findings and backups peak in the two weeks after each major festival, four times a year.
Temporary food vendors operate during festivals without interceptor requirements.
Permanent premises keep compliant interceptors year round and their laterals stay clean.
Between festivals, the district sewers run clean for months.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Permanent premises interceptors fail during festivals from overload
Temporary vendors are the seasonal grease source, because permanent laterals stay clean and problems exist only in festival periods
Tourist water use alone deposits the grease
Cleaning crews take holidays after festivals, causing the pattern

inference.explanation: Permanent laterals stay clean through the same festivals, sewers run clean between events, and the only uncontrolled discharge appears with the temporary vendors. Water use carries no grease by itself, and no cleaning gap is reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: CCTV of vendor area laterals and permanent laterals during and after a festival
Permanent premises service records alone
Tourist visitor counts

nextClue.explanation: Comparing vendor and permanent laterals in the same festival isolates the uncontrolled source.

clueText.nc-a: Vendor laterals coat with fresh grease during the festival while permanent laterals stay clean.
clueText.nc-b: Permanent records are already compliant and cannot explain festival only fouling.
clueText.nc-c: Visitor counts show crowds, not which discharge carries grease.

tasks.prompt: Two operators code the same video very differently, and a review explains why.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: Operator 1 codes many fine cracks along a concrete reach.
Operator 2 codes the same features as surface crazing with no structural cracks.
A zoomed still review shows the lines do not open, displace, or leak, and follow a surface pattern.
A calibration reach with known defects is coded accurately by both operators.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Operator 1 is correct because more coding is always safer
The features are surface crazing, and the difference is interpretation of fine lines, not eyesight, since both code the calibration reach well
The video quality changed between the two viewings
Crazing and cracks are the same defect for grading

inference.explanation: Both operators prove competent on the calibration reach, and zoomed stills show unopened surface pattern lines with no displacement or leakage. Coding those as structural cracks overstates condition. The distinction matters because grades drive renewal spending.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Zoomed still set from the disputed chainages, reviewed jointly against the coding definitions
Operator seniority records
Video file size and playback speed

nextClue.explanation: Joint still review against definitions settles what the features are, which seniority cannot.

clueText.nc-a: The joint review classifies the lines as crazing and both operators agree once the stills are examined.
clueText.nc-b: Seniority does not change what the stills show.
clueText.nc-c: Playback details do not alter the defect appearance on stills.

tasks.prompt: A CCTV run in a surcharged pipe produces a severe grade that a reviewer questions.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: The run was done with flow covering the lower two thirds of the pipe.
The operator coded wall defects and joint condition for the full circumference.
Only the crown was visible above the waterline for most of the run.
A later run at low flow shows sound joints and walls in the same reach.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pipe repaired itself between runs
The first grade coded surfaces the camera could not see, so only the low flow run can support a full circumference grade
The second crew was less thorough
Surcharged runs give better grades because flow cleans the walls

inference.explanation: Two thirds of the pipe was underwater and invisible, yet full circumference defects were coded. The low flow run that could actually see the pipe found it sound. A grade can only rest on observed surfaces.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Waterline depth log for the first run, with the low flow video for the same chainages
Operator work schedules
Flow records for the street alone

nextClue.explanation: The waterline log proves how much of the first run was unobservable, and the second video supplies the real condition.

clueText.nc-a: The log confirms the lower two thirds were submerged, and the low flow run shows the sound pipe the first grade missed.
clueText.nc-b: Schedules do not show what was visible on camera.
clueText.nc-c: Flow records explain the surcharge but not the coding of hidden surfaces.

tasks.prompt: An offset joint is coded as a collapse risk, and measurements are checked.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: The joint is offset by about half the pipe wall thickness, with no soil visible and no flow disturbance.
Pipe above and below the joint is round, aligned, and free of cracks.
The same offset measurement is unchanged in CCTV runs five years apart.
No surface depression exists above the joint.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Any offset joint will collapse soon and needs emergency repair
A stable half thickness offset with no soil loss, cracking, or surface sign over five years is a minor defect to monitor, not an emergency
The offset must have happened in the last year
Flow passing smoothly proves the joint is fully sound and needs no record

inference.explanation: Severity comes from progression and consequences, and here nothing has changed in five years, no soil is entering, and the surface is intact. That is a monitor level defect. Calling it fully sound goes too far the other way, an offset is still a recorded defect.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: The two CCTV runs five years apart, measured at the same joint with the same reference
Emergency repair cost estimates
Surface photographs alone

nextClue.explanation: Repeat measurement over time is what separates a stable minor defect from an active failure.

clueText.nc-a: Both runs measure the same half thickness offset with no new cracking or soil, confirming stability.
clueText.nc-b: Cost estimates assume the emergency that the measurements do not support.
clueText.nc-c: Surface photos alone cannot measure joint movement.

tasks.prompt: Deposits are coded as reducing a pipe diameter by half, and a flow check disagrees.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: CCTV coding reports deposits occupying 50 percent of the diameter along a reach.
Measured flow capacity of the reach matches a clean pipe of that size at the same slope.
A still frame review shows the deposit estimate came from one frame at a manhole outlet where material piles locally.
Frames along the reach show thin deposits of about 10 percent elsewhere.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The flow measurement must be wrong because CCTV is always right
One local pile at the outlet was generalised to the whole reach, overstating deposits that are thin elsewhere and consistent with full capacity
Deposits reduce capacity without reducing measured flow
The reach should be lined based on the 50 percent coding

inference.explanation: Capacity measurement agrees with the thin deposits seen along the reach, not with a half blocked pipe. The single outlet frame explains the coding error, a local pile read as a reach condition. Lining on that coding would spend renewal money on a measurement mistake.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Frame by frame deposit estimates along the reach, with the capacity test result
The original coding summary alone
Liner design drawings for the reach

nextClue.explanation: Frame by frame estimates show whether the outlet pile represents the reach or stands alone.

clueText.nc-a: Estimates sit near 10 percent for the full reach and jump only in the outlet frame, matching the capacity test.
clueText.nc-b: The summary repeats the single generalised value being questioned.
clueText.nc-c: Design drawings act on the coding rather than testing it.

tasks.prompt: A longitudinal crack is tracked across three CCTV cycles to set a renewal date.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: Cycle 1, eight years ago, shows a hairline longitudinal crack over 3 m.
Cycle 2, four years ago, shows the same crack slightly open with fine roots entering.
Cycle 3, this year, shows the crack open wider, with soil visible and a small crown deformation.
Flow and surface condition above the pipe are still normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The crack has been stable and can be ignored for another decade
The crack is progressing through clear stages, roots, opening, soil visibility and deformation, so renewal should be scheduled before structural failure
Roots entering a crack prove the pipe is self healing
Normal flow means the structure is sound

inference.explanation: Each cycle adds a progression marker, and the latest adds soil visibility and deformation, which are structural warnings. Normal flow only says the bore is open today. Waiting for failure ignores a documented eight year trend.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: The three cycle image set at the same chainages, with crack width and deformation notes
Flow records for the reach
Surface photographs of the road above

nextClue.explanation: The dated image series is the direct evidence of progression rate that sets the renewal window.

clueText.nc-a: Widths and deformation increase at each cycle, projecting loss of soil support within the next cycle interval.
clueText.nc-b: Flow stays normal in many failing pipes until late collapse.
clueText.nc-c: Surface photos are still normal, which is why the camera trend matters.

tasks.prompt: Manhole condition assessment finds benching failure as the main defect in a group of structures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: Pipe runs entering the manholes grade as sound.
Benching in most structures is cracked and missing chunks, and flow splashes onto the bench instead of following the channel.
Debris accumulates on the broken benching and is the source of repeated downstream ragging complaints.
Walls and covers of the same structures are in fair condition.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pipes need lining because debris is found downstream
The defect is at the structures, where broken benching traps and releases debris, so manhole rehabilitation is the correct scope
Debris complaints mean the whole catchment needs more jetting only
Fair walls mean the manholes need no work at all

inference.explanation: Pipes are sound, walls are fair, and the broken benching is both observed and mechanically linked to debris release downstream. Lining sound pipes would miss the defect, and jetting treats the symptom the benching keeps recreating.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Manhole inspection photographs of benching and channel, with the downstream debris findings
Pipe lining proposals for the entering sewers
Jetting frequency records alone

nextClue.explanation: Structure photographs paired with downstream findings tie the debris source to the benching condition.

clueText.nc-a: Photographs show missing benching sections exactly where debris collects, and repaired trial structures stopped releasing debris.
clueText.nc-b: Proposals line pipes that already grade sound.
clueText.nc-c: Jetting records show effort, not the source creating the debris.

tasks.prompt: A protruding lateral is coded, and its effect is confirmed by debris patterns.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: CCTV shows a service connection protruding 50 mm into the main.
Wipes and paper drape on the protrusion in every run, while neighbouring connections sit flush.
Blockages on the reach always occur at or just below this connection.
After the protrusion is trimmed, the reach runs a full year with no blockage.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The protrusion is harmless because the pipe still has most of its bore
The protrusion snags debris and starts the blockages, proven by the draping, the fixed location, and the clear year after trimming
Blockages at that spot are caused by roots further down
One clear year after trimming is too short to conclude anything, so the cause is unknown

inference.explanation: Debris drapes on the protrusion itself, blockages fix at its location, flush neighbours cause no trouble, and trimming ends the pattern for a year. That is a complete cause chain. Roots further down are not reported on any run.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Before and after CCTV at the connection, with blockage locations mapped by chainage
Root defect logs for the downstream reach
Pipe diameter measurements alone

nextClue.explanation: Chainage mapped blockages with the before and after camera views close the case on the protrusion.

clueText.nc-a: All mapped blockages sit within 2 m of the connection, and the after view shows a flush trimmed opening with no draping.
clueText.nc-b: No root defects are logged downstream.
clueText.nc-c: Diameter alone ignores the snagging mechanism the camera shows.

tasks.prompt: Infiltration coding from a dry season CCTV run understates a reach, and a wet season run is ordered.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: The dry season run codes no infiltration anywhere in the reach.
Flow monitoring shows strong wet season night flow gains in the same reach.
A wet season run shows joint infiltration at many joints, with mineral deposits marking the entry points.
Mineral deposits were visible but not coded as infiltration evidence in the dry run.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The reach has no infiltration because the first run saw none
Infiltration is seasonal with the water table, so dry season coding missed active entry that mineral deposits already hinted at
The wet season run defects are camera artefacts
Flow gains come from a different reach

inference.explanation: Flow data place the gains in this reach, the wet run sees the entry directly, and mineral deposits in the dry run were the standing evidence of past infiltration. Seasonal water table movement explains why a dry run can look clean. Assessment timing must match the condition being measured.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Wet and dry season video pair for the same joints, with the flow monitoring reach boundaries
Dry season coding summary alone
Camera maintenance records

nextClue.explanation: The paired seasonal runs at the same joints prove the timing effect and correct the reach record.

clueText.nc-a: Joints dry in summer stream in spring, and mineral staining marks the same joints in both runs.
clueText.nc-b: The dry summary is the incomplete record being corrected.
clueText.nc-c: Maintenance records do not explain joint by joint seasonal streaming.

tasks.prompt: A CCTV program reports kilometres completed, but a data audit finds repeat runs inflating progress.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: Reported completion is 90 percent of the network in three years.
The audit finds 25 percent of the runs are repeats of the same easy access reaches.
High priority older reaches near the river have never been televised.
Repeat runs were logged as new production each time.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The program is 90 percent complete as reported
True first time coverage is much lower, because repeat production was counted as new, and the highest risk reaches remain uninspected
Repeat runs are worth the same as first runs for condition knowledge
The river reaches can be assumed sound because they have no complaints

inference.explanation: Counting repeats as new production overstates coverage, and the uninspected reaches are the oldest and highest risk. Repeat runs add little condition knowledge, and no complaints is not evidence of condition in pipes that have never been seen.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: A chainage level coverage map showing first runs, repeats, and never inspected reaches
The program annual production totals
Complaint records for the river reaches

nextClue.explanation: A coverage map is the only view that separates real first time inspection from repeated production.

clueText.nc-a: The map shows true first time coverage near 65 percent, with the river reaches blank.
clueText.nc-b: Totals are the inflated figures the audit is questioning.
clueText.nc-c: Complaint absence cannot grade pipes that have never been televised.

tasks.prompt: A fracture is coded at a pipe joint, and a second look shows a factory mark instead.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV condition program. Coding uses generic defect descriptions, not a proprietary code set.

evidence.label: The coded fracture is a straight dark line crossing the joint at a regular angle.
Identical lines appear at every joint in the same pipe run at the same position.
No opening, displacement, leakage, or soil is visible at any of the lines.
The pipe supplier confirms a mould seam mark is cast at that position on this pipe type.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Every joint in the run is fractured in the same way
The lines are a repeating factory seam mark, not fractures, because real fractures do not repeat identically with no opening or leakage
The supplier is covering up a defective product
The lines will become fractures, so coding them as fractures now is correct

inference.explanation: Identical marks at every joint, confirmed as a cast seam, with no fracture behaviour at any of them, cannot be a run of identical fractures. Future risk does not justify coding a present defect that is not there, grades must record observed condition.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Still images from several joints in the run, with the supplier pipe specification
The original coding report alone
A pressure test of one joint

nextClue.explanation: Repetition across joints plus the specification identifies the mark, which a single joint test cannot.

clueText.nc-a: All joints show the identical seam at the same clock position, matching the specification drawing.
clueText.nc-b: The report is the coding under review, not independent evidence.
clueText.nc-c: One joint test says nothing about a mark repeated at every joint.

tasks.prompt: A flow monitor reports a flat line at one value for five days, including a major storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: The reported flow holds at exactly 24.0 L/s with no variation, day or night.
Rainfall records show a 28 mm storm on day three.
Upstream and downstream monitors both show normal diurnal patterns and a storm peak.
A site visit finds the depth sensor cable disconnected and the logger holding its last value.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The catchment flow is unusually stable
The monitor has failed and is reporting a held value, because real flow cannot ignore nights and a major storm that neighbours recorded
The storm missed this catchment only
Both neighbouring monitors are faulty in the same way

inference.explanation: A perfectly flat line through nights and a storm that two neighbouring monitors recorded is not a flow pattern, it is an instrument state. The disconnected cable found on site completes the explanation. Data from the period must be flagged, not analysed.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Logger diagnostic record and the neighbouring monitor hydrographs for the same five days
Catchment water use records
Rainfall gauge calibration records

nextClue.explanation: Neighbour hydrographs prove what real flow did while the diagnostics show why this monitor did not record it.

clueText.nc-a: Neighbours show the storm peak and diurnal cycle the flat monitor missed, and diagnostics confirm the sensor loss time.
clueText.nc-b: Water use cannot flatten flow through a major storm.
clueText.nc-c: Gauge calibration does not explain a held logger value.

tasks.prompt: A velocity meter reads low after a storm, and depth readings stay correct.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: Depth readings match a staff gauge at every check before and after the storm.
Velocity readings after the storm are about half the pre storm values at the same depths.
Inspection finds a mat of rags and silt covering the velocity sensor face.
A temporary meter beside the site reads normal velocities at the same depths.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Flow in the sewer halved after the storm at the same depth
The fouled velocity sensor under reads, so flows computed since the storm are understated while depths remain valid
The staff gauge and temporary meter are both wrong
The pipe area changed during the storm

inference.explanation: Depth is verified two ways and velocity is contradicted by a temporary meter at the same depths. The fouled sensor face is the physical cause. Flow at the same depth in the same pipe cannot halve without a velocity change that the clean meter does not see.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sensor inspection photographs with the temporary meter comparison at matched depths
The original meter flow totals for the storm week
Pipe design drawings

nextClue.explanation: Matched depth comparison with a clean meter isolates the velocity error and dates it to the fouling event.

clueText.nc-a: At matched depths the fouled meter reads half the temporary meter, and cleaning the face restores agreement.
clueText.nc-b: The totals are the suspect output, not evidence.
clueText.nc-c: Drawings confirm the area the temporary meter already used correctly.

tasks.prompt: Two monitors on one trunk disagree by a steady percentage at all flows.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: Monitor X reads 20 percent above Monitor Y at low, medium, and high flows.
Both depth sensors agree with staff gauge checks.
Monitor X uses a pipe diameter of 750 mm in its setup, the installed pipe is 675 mm, which Monitor Y uses.
Swapping the loggers between sites moves the disagreement with the setup, not the site.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: One sewer reach gains 20 percent flow between the monitors
Monitor X overstates flow because its area is computed from the wrong diameter, a setup error that scales every reading
Monitor Y velocity sensor is fouled
The trunk leaks 20 percent of flow past Monitor Y

inference.explanation: The error is a constant percentage, depths verify, and the fault follows the setup when loggers swap. A wrong diameter inflates area and therefore every computed flow by a fixed ratio. Fouling or leakage would not follow a logger swap or hold a perfect percentage at all flows.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Setup audit for both monitors, with area calculations from the as built diameter
Leak detection survey for the trunk reach
Velocity sensor cleaning records

nextClue.explanation: The setup audit with the swap result proves the error lives in configuration, not in the sewer.

clueText.nc-a: Correcting X to 675 mm brings the two monitors into agreement across the full flow range.
clueText.nc-b: No leak is found, and a leak could not follow a logger swap.
clueText.nc-c: Cleaning records are irrelevant once the swap isolates the setup.

tasks.prompt: A monitor shows flow spikes every day at the same hour that field staff cannot explain.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: Spikes of about 30 L/s last ten minutes at 6 in the morning daily, with no matching rise at the downstream monitor.
Depth at the site barely changes during the spikes, while velocity jumps sharply.
The site is below a bridge where a maintenance crew washes equipment at 6 in the morning, sending a jet of water past the sensor.
On holidays, when no washing occurs, the spikes are absent.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A daily industrial discharge enters at 6 in the morning
The wash water jet crossing the velocity sensor creates false spikes, because depth and downstream flow do not rise
The downstream monitor misses the spikes because they are too short
Residents all flush at the same minute each morning

inference.explanation: A real discharge would raise depth and arrive downstream. Neither happens, while a water jet crosses the sensor at exactly the spike time and spikes vanish on holidays. The instrument is being disturbed locally, not measuring catchment flow.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Site observation during the 6 in the morning wash, with depth and downstream records for the same minutes
Industrial discharge permits for the catchment
Resident water use surveys

nextClue.explanation: Direct observation with the paired records shows the jet producing the spike with no real flow change.

clueText.nc-a: The spike starts and stops with the wash jet while depth and downstream flow stay flat.
clueText.nc-b: No permitted discharge matches the daily ten minute pattern.
clueText.nc-c: Surveys cannot produce a depth free velocity spike.

tasks.prompt: Night flow data from a monitor are used for an I and I study, but a drift is found.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: Zero checks show the depth sensor drifting upward by 2 mm per week over the study.
Reported night flows rise slowly across the study in every basin using that sensor model and setup.
A basin with a different sensor type shows flat night flows over the same period.
Recalibrated sensors reinstalled mid study immediately report lower night flows.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Infiltration rose slowly in all the drift affected basins during the study
Sensor drift inflated the night flow trend, because the rise follows the instrument, disappears on recalibration, and is absent on a different sensor
Groundwater rose under all basins that season
The recalibration was done incorrectly in the same way everywhere

inference.explanation: The trend follows the sensor model, is explained by measured zero drift, reverses on recalibration, and is absent where a different sensor ran. Groundwater would not respect sensor brands or step down at recalibration.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Zero check and recalibration records by site, with night flow trends split by sensor type
Groundwater well records for the study area
Study night flow averages alone

nextClue.explanation: Splitting trends by sensor type is the decisive test, because a real groundwater rise would appear on all instruments.

clueText.nc-a: Only drift affected sites show the rise, and each drops at its own recalibration date.
clueText.nc-b: Wells show no matching rise for the period.
clueText.nc-c: Averages blend the faulty and sound sites together.

tasks.prompt: A monitor downstream of a lift station reports flows that exceed the pump capacity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: The monitor reports peaks 40 percent above the combined rated capacity of the station pumps.
Station run records show normal cycle times and no surcharge during the reported peaks.
The monitor depth sensor is mounted above a drop in the manhole, where falling water entrains air and foam.
A portable meter in the next manhole downstream reports peaks within pump capacity.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pumps outperform their rating by 40 percent
Foam and entrained air at the drop are corrupting the depth reading, overstating flow at the monitor site
The portable meter is faulty
The station records under report the true cycles

inference.explanation: Pumps cannot exceed their combined capacity by 40 percent with normal cycles and no surcharge, and a clean downstream site reads within capacity. The drop, foam, and air at the sensor explain a site specific over read.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Portable meter comparison at both manholes across several pump cycles
Pump rating curves alone
Station cycle records alone

nextClue.explanation: Simultaneous comparison across cycles shows whether the error lives at the drop site or in the flow itself.

clueText.nc-a: The portable meter agrees with pump capacity at both sites once moved away from the drop foam, while the fixed site over reads on every cycle.
clueText.nc-b: Rating curves state capacity but not which meter is wrong.
clueText.nc-c: Cycle records support the capacity limit but cannot locate the sensor fault.

tasks.prompt: Rainfall data for a flow study come from a gauge 8 km away, and results look wrong for one basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: The distant gauge records 30 mm for a storm, while two local gauges near the basin record 12 mm.
Basin flow response matches the local gauges in timing and size.
Other basins near the distant gauge match its 30 mm response well.
Summer storms in the area are known to be localised convective cells.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The basin has an unusually weak response to rainfall
The distant gauge misrepresents rain over this basin for localised storms, so RDII computed from it understates the basin response
The basin flow monitor under reads during storms
Local gauges are both faulty in the same way

inference.explanation: Flow matches the two independent local gauges, and distant basins match the distant gauge. In localised summer storms, rainfall varies over kilometres, so one remote gauge cannot serve every basin. Two gauges agreeing against one distant gauge also rules out a shared local fault.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Local and distant gauge comparison for several storms, with basin response per millimetre from each source
The flow monitor calibration record
Annual rainfall maps for the region

nextClue.explanation: Response per millimetre from each gauge shows which rainfall source the basin flow actually follows.

clueText.nc-a: Basin response is consistent storm to storm using local rain and erratic using distant rain.
clueText.nc-b: Calibration is sound, and the monitor matches local rain timing.
clueText.nc-c: Annual maps smooth out the storm scale variation that causes the problem.

tasks.prompt: A level sensor in a surcharge prone manhole tops out during the biggest events.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: The sensor range ends 0.5 m below the manhole rim.
During the two largest storms, the record holds at the range limit for over an hour.
Staff gauge readings during one event show the level 0.3 m above the sensor limit.
Smaller events record normally with clear peaks below the limit.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The surcharge level truly plateaus at the sensor limit in big storms
The biggest events exceed the sensor range, so peak levels and durations above the limit are missing from the record
The manhole rim is lower than surveyed
Staff gauge readings during storms are unreliable by nature

inference.explanation: The record clips at exactly the instrument limit while a direct staff reading goes above it. A natural plateau at the precise range limit, twice, is not credible. Any analysis of peak surcharge from this record understates the worst events.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sensor range specification with the event records and the staff gauge reading for the same storm
Manhole rim survey alone
Records from the smaller events alone

nextClue.explanation: The specification against the clipped records proves the data gap, and the staff reading shows how far above it the water went.

clueText.nc-a: Both large events clip at the limit while the staff gauge reads 0.3 m higher, confirming lost peak data.
clueText.nc-b: The rim survey does not change the sensor range limit.
clueText.nc-c: Smaller events never reach the limit, so they cannot reveal the clipping.

tasks.prompt: Flow data show a step change the day a monitor is serviced, with no change in the sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: Reported flows drop 15 percent in one step on the service date and hold at the new level.
The service replaced a worn sensor mounting that had held the sensor 20 mm off its surveyed position.
Upstream and downstream monitors show no step on that date.
No sewer work, connections, or diversions occurred that week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Catchment flow genuinely fell 15 percent on the service day
The old mounting offset had biased readings, and the step marks the correction, so data before and after are not directly comparable
The new sensor is faulty and under reads
A diversion opened upstream on the same day by coincidence

inference.explanation: The step aligns exactly with a documented mounting correction, neighbours show no step, and nothing changed in the catchment. A real 15 percent flow change with no cause and no neighbour response is not supported. Trend studies must split the record at the service date.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Service report with the mounting measurements, and the three monitor trends across the date
Catchment connection records for the week
New sensor factory certificate alone

nextClue.explanation: The service measurements explain the step size and direction, which a certificate alone cannot.

clueText.nc-a: The 20 mm offset accounts for the bias, and corrected readings agree with the downstream monitor from the service date.
clueText.nc-b: No connections or diversions are recorded that week.
clueText.nc-c: A factory certificate does not address the field mounting error that was found.

tasks.prompt: A study averages flow over 15 minute intervals and misses the true storm peak.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow monitoring deployment. Instrument and field check results are as stated.

evidence.label: Raw one minute data show a sharp peak lasting about six minutes during an intense storm burst.
The 15 minute averaged record reports a peak 35 percent lower for the same event.
Dry weather flows agree between the raw and averaged records.
The sewer is a small, fast responding catchment where peaks are brief.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The raw sensor overshoots during intense rain
Averaging over 15 minutes smooths a six minute peak, understating the design peak for a fast catchment
The averaged record is the more accurate peak
Dry weather agreement proves the averaging is fine for storms too

inference.explanation: Averaging cannot create or remove water, it redistributes it in time, which lowers short peaks and matches dry weather where flow is steady. In a fast catchment the true peak lives inside one averaging window. Design work needs the raw interval data.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Raw and averaged hydrographs for the same storm, with the peak duration marked
Dry weather comparison alone
Logger battery records

nextClue.explanation: Overlaying the two records for the storm shows the smoothing directly at the peak.

clueText.nc-a: The raw peak sits inside a single averaged interval and the averaged value falls between the peak and its shoulders.
clueText.nc-b: Dry weather is steady, so it cannot reveal peak smoothing.
clueText.nc-c: Battery records do not affect interval mathematics.

tasks.prompt: A trunk surcharges at one manhole while the pipe downstream runs half full.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: Level loggers show the surcharge begins at a manhole where a 600 mm sewer joins a 450 mm sewer.
Downstream of the smaller pipe, levels are normal and the pipe runs half full.
The smaller section was a utility crossing sleeve installed decades ago and never upsized.
Upstream levels rise only when flow exceeds the smaller section capacity.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The downstream trunk is blocked and backing up
The short smaller section is a bottleneck that surcharges the upstream manhole once its capacity is passed, while downstream stays free
The upstream catchment produces too much flow for the whole trunk
The level logger at the surcharge manhole is faulty

inference.explanation: Downstream is half full, which rules out a downstream blockage or a whole trunk overload. Levels rise at the size change and only above the smaller section capacity. The sleeve is the restriction, and the logger pattern matches its location.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Level records above, at, and below the size change during a surcharge event
Downstream CCTV survey alone
Catchment flow estimates alone

nextClue.explanation: Three point levels during an event locate the restriction to the section where levels break.

clueText.nc-a: Levels back up above the sleeve and stay normal below it in the same event.
clueText.nc-b: A downstream survey looks where levels already show free flow.
clueText.nc-c: Estimates cannot locate a restriction inside the trunk.

tasks.prompt: Basement backups cluster in homes served by one branch during storms, while the trunk has spare capacity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: The trunk runs at 60 percent depth during the backup storms.
The branch serving the affected homes runs surcharged from its junction with a flat, silted reach.
CCTV shows the flat reach half filled with silt along 80 m.
Homes on a parallel branch with a clean, steeper reach have no backups in the same storms.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The trunk is undersized for storm flow
The silted flat branch loses half its bore and surcharges locally, backing up its homes while the trunk still has room
The affected homes all have plumbing faults
Storm inflow is higher over this branch only

inference.explanation: The trunk has spare depth, the parallel branch is fine in the same storms, and the affected branch contains an 80 m reach half lost to silt. Local capacity loss explains local backups. Many simultaneous plumbing faults are not credible.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Depth records in the trunk and both branches during a backup storm, with the CCTV silt profile
Home plumbing inspection offers
Rainfall records by street

nextClue.explanation: Simultaneous depths show whether surcharge is born in the branch while the trunk stays free.

clueText.nc-a: The silted branch surcharges from the flat reach upward while the trunk and clean branch stay below 70 percent.
clueText.nc-b: Inspections would test homes, not the branch condition already on camera.
clueText.nc-c: Rainfall is the same over both branches in these storms.

tasks.prompt: Surcharge appears only when two upstream lift stations discharge at the same time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: Each station alone raises trunk depth to about 50 percent.
When both discharge together, depth reaches the soffit and one low manhole surcharges.
Station controls start both pumps on independent level signals with no coordination.
On days when starts happen to stagger, no surcharge occurs at the same total daily flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Each station is oversized for the trunk on its own
Coincident discharge peaks stack in the trunk and exceed its capacity, so staggering starts is a direct remedy
The trunk has a blockage that appears only on some days
Daily flow growth has exceeded trunk capacity at all hours

inference.explanation: Solo running is safe, staggered days at the same total flow are safe, and only coincident peaks surcharge. That timing dependence identifies peak stacking, not a fixed blockage or all day overload. Coordinating starts attacks the exact mechanism.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Trunk depth record aligned with both station pump status logs for surcharge and non surcharge days
Trunk CCTV survey
Daily total flow records alone

nextClue.explanation: Alignment of depth with pump status across both day types proves the coincidence mechanism.

clueText.nc-a: Surcharge minutes match double discharge minutes exactly, and staggered days peak at 70 percent depth.
clueText.nc-b: CCTV shows no blockage that could appear and disappear by the hour.
clueText.nc-c: Daily totals are equal on both day types, so totals cannot explain the difference.

tasks.prompt: A surcharge investigation finds the cause is a tide and river gate, not pipe capacity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: The outfall flap gate is found jammed half closed by debris.
Sewer levels near the outfall rise with river level, even in dry weather high river periods.
Upstream reaches far from the outfall keep normal levels during the same periods.
After the gate is cleared, levels near the outfall stop tracking the river.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lower trunk is undersized and must be replaced
The jammed gate lets river head back the sewer up, and clearing it removes the surcharge without pipe work
Groundwater infiltration explains levels tracking the river
Dry weather river tracking is a level logger artefact

inference.explanation: Levels track the river in dry weather, only near the outfall, and stop when the jammed gate is cleared. Infiltration would not switch off with gate clearing, and an undersized trunk would not follow river level on dry days.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Level records near and far from the outfall against river level, before and after gate clearing
Trunk upsizing design drawings
Logger calibration records

nextClue.explanation: The before and after river tracking comparison is the cleanest proof the gate was the driver.

clueText.nc-a: Before clearing, outfall levels mirror the river, after clearing they hold a normal dry weather profile at the same river levels.
clueText.nc-b: Drawings plan a replacement the gate result may make unnecessary.
clueText.nc-c: Calibration is fine, since far loggers behaved normally throughout.

tasks.prompt: Homes back up in moderate rain after a new subdivision connects upstream.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: Pre connection, the trunk peaked at 70 percent depth in the design storm.
Post connection, the same size storm peaks at the soffit and low homes back up.
The subdivision was approved with a flow allowance equal to the spare 30 percent, but its built density is 40 percent higher than the approved plan.
No new defects or blockages are found on CCTV of the trunk.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The trunk deteriorated at the same time as the connection
Built flows exceed the approved allowance and consume more than the spare capacity, surcharging the trunk in storms it used to pass
The backup homes developed lateral faults together
Rainfall has become more intense since the connection

inference.explanation: The pipe is clean on camera, storms are matched, and the only change is built density 40 percent above the allowance that was sized to the spare capacity. The arithmetic of allowance versus spare room explains the lost margin.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Approved allowance and as built connection counts, with trunk depth records for matched storms before and after
Lateral inspection program for the backup homes
Rainfall intensity trend analysis

nextClue.explanation: Matched storm depths with the allowance audit show whether demand growth, not pipe condition, took the spare capacity.

clueText.nc-a: As built flows exceed the allowance by the same margin that depths rose, and matched storms confirm the change.
clueText.nc-b: Lateral faults would not raise trunk depth to the soffit.
clueText.nc-c: Matched storms remove rainfall trend from the comparison.

tasks.prompt: Surcharge happens in winter storms but not in larger summer storms in the same catchment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: Winter surcharge events occur during rain on frozen ground with snowmelt adding flow.
Larger summer storms on dry, unfrozen ground produce lower peaks in the same sewers.
Roof leaders and catchbasin connections in the catchment are extensive.
Flow records show winter events have both higher peaks and much longer high flow durations.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Summer rainfall gauges under record large storms
Frozen ground and snowmelt turn almost all precipitation into inflow, so smaller winter events deliver more water to the sewer than larger summer events
Pipes shrink in winter and lose capacity
Winter surcharge is caused by ice forming inside the sewers

inference.explanation: Winter events combine rain, melt, and frozen ground that cannot absorb water, giving higher and longer inflow through the many direct connections. Summer rain partly soaks away. Pipe size does not change with season, and no internal ice is reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Precipitation, snowmelt, and temperature records with flow hydrographs for matched winter and summer events
Pipe diameter measurements in both seasons
Internal ice inspection reports

nextClue.explanation: Full water input accounting, rain plus melt on frozen ground, is what the summer comparison omits.

clueText.nc-a: Total winter water input exceeds the summer storm input once melt is added, matching the higher and longer flows.
clueText.nc-b: Diameters are the same in both seasons.
clueText.nc-c: No ice is found inside the sewers during winter events.

tasks.prompt: A single low home backs up in storms while its street sewer never surcharges.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: Street manholes stay below the soffit in all recorded storms.
The home is the lowest on the street, with a basement floor below the manhole rim level.
Its lateral is long, flat, and found half blocked by roots at the property line.
During storms, street depth rises enough to submerge the lateral outlet for hours.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The street sewer surcharges and the loggers miss it
The flat, root restricted lateral cannot drain against a submerged outlet during long high street depths, so the home backs up without a street surcharge
The home plumbing vent is blocked
Neighbours are also backing up but not reporting it

inference.explanation: The street never reaches surcharge, yet the outlet sits submerged for hours and the lateral is flat and half blocked, so the home cannot discharge and its own flow backs up. That is a lateral hydraulics problem, not a main surcharge. Vent faults do not follow storm depth timing.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Lateral camera log with street depth records for the same storms
Additional street level loggers
Neighbour complaint survey alone

nextClue.explanation: Pairing the lateral condition with outlet submergence during storms explains a single home pattern the street record cannot.

clueText.nc-a: The lateral holds water at the root restriction whenever the outlet is submerged, and drains freely at low street depth.
clueText.nc-b: More street loggers would confirm what records already show, no surcharge.
clueText.nc-c: A survey cannot show the lateral hydraulics that the camera records.

tasks.prompt: Surcharge relief from a storage tank is less than designed, and the shortfall is traced.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: The tank fills only to 60 percent during events that still surcharge upstream.
Its inlet is set higher than the design drawing, so flow enters late in each event.
The upstream surcharge begins before the tank starts filling.
Tank outlet and controls work as designed once filling begins.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The tank is too small and must be enlarged
The high inlet wastes the first part of every event and 40 percent of the volume, so correcting the inlet level recovers the design relief
Upstream inflow exceeds the design storm in every event
The outlet controls are throttling the filling

inference.explanation: The tank never gets the chance to use its full volume because its inlet sits above design level, and surcharge starts before any filling. Enlarging a tank that cannot fill would repeat the error. Outlet behaviour is verified normal once filling starts.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: As built inlet level survey against the design drawing, with tank level and upstream surcharge timing
Tank enlargement cost estimates
Design storm rainfall records alone

nextClue.explanation: The level survey plus event timing shows the lost volume is an inlet setting problem, not a size problem.

clueText.nc-a: The inlet sits 0.4 m high, surcharge precedes filling in every event, and modelling the corrected level uses the full tank.
clueText.nc-b: Estimates price a bigger tank before the existing one is shown to fill.
clueText.nc-c: Rainfall records do not explain filling that starts after surcharge.

tasks.prompt: A sewer surcharges at night in dry weather after an industrial user expands.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: Dry weather night levels in the industrial area sewer began rising after the plant expansion.
The plant now discharges its process batch at night to avoid daytime fees, by its own discharge log.
Night flow in the sewer matches the batch volume and timing in the log.
Residential night flow in a parallel sewer is unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residents changed their night water use at the same time
The night batch discharge fills the sewer in otherwise low flow hours, causing the dry weather night surcharge
Infiltration rises only at night in this catchment
The level logger drifts upward at night

inference.explanation: The rise starts with the expansion, matches the plant own batch log in volume and timing, and is absent in the residential parallel sewer. Infiltration does not follow a discharge log, and a drifting logger would not match batch volumes.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Plant discharge log aligned with sewer flow and level records at night
Residential night use survey
Logger zero check records

nextClue.explanation: Alignment with the plant log is the direct attribution test for a scheduled discharge.

clueText.nc-a: Every night surcharge matches a logged batch, and a plant shutdown weekend shows normal low night levels.
clueText.nc-b: Residential use is flat in the parallel sewer over the same nights.
clueText.nc-c: Zero checks are clean, and drift would not pause for a shutdown weekend.

tasks.prompt: After a relief sewer is built, the old trunk still surcharges at one location.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge investigation. Level, flow and rainfall records are as stated.

evidence.label: The relief sewer carries its design share of flow in storms.
The old trunk runs at moderate depth everywhere except one reach below a large roof leader cluster.
That reach receives inflow from a parking lot drain connected after the relief design was set.
Removing that connection in a trial eliminates the local surcharge.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The relief sewer was built too small
A later local connection added inflow the relief design never allowed for, creating a local surcharge the trial removal confirms
The old trunk has a hidden collapse in that reach
The relief sewer is blocked and sending flow back

inference.explanation: The relief performs to design, the surcharge is local to one reach, a post design connection is identified there, and removing it in trial ends the surcharge. A collapse would not be cured by disconnecting a drain, and the relief flows disprove a relief blockage.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Flow split records between the trunks, with the connection history and trial result for the reach
Relief sewer CCTV survey
Old trunk collapse investigation proposal

nextClue.explanation: The trial removal result is the decisive experiment, it removes exactly the added inflow and the surcharge with it.

clueText.nc-a: With the drain disconnected, the reach peaks at 70 percent in the same size storm that previously surcharged it.
clueText.nc-b: The relief CCTV is clean and its flows already match design.
clueText.nc-c: A collapse investigation is overtaken by the successful trial.

tasks.prompt: Smoke testing finds one home with smoke in its yard, and follow up isolates the defect.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Smoke appears from the ground beside the home foundation during testing of the street main.
No smoke appears inside the home or at its roof vent.
Excavation by camera from the cleanout shows the lateral cracked and open 1 m from the foundation.
Neighbouring laterals on the same test show smoke only at their roof vents.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The home plumbing is leaking smoke indoors
The cracked lateral beside the foundation is venting smoke to the yard and admitting soil water in wet weather
Smoke in a yard always means a main defect
The test pressure was too high and created the crack

inference.explanation: Smoke at the ground beside the foundation, none indoors, and a camera showing an open crack at that spot form one consistent picture. Neighbours vent normally at roofs, so test pressure is not cracking sound laterals. The main is not where the camera found the opening.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Lateral camera log with the smoke test record for the same property
Main CCTV for the street alone
Test pressure gauge certificate

nextClue.explanation: The lateral log ties the surface smoke to the exact defect that needs repair.

clueText.nc-a: The crack sits at the smoke location, and dye placed in the soil above it appears in the lateral during wetting.
clueText.nc-b: Main CCTV cannot locate a defect inside a private lateral.
clueText.nc-c: Pressure was within the standard range used on all homes in the test.

tasks.prompt: A sump pump connection study uses pump run data to size a disconnection program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: During a storm, flow in one street sewer rises in repeated ten minute pulses.
The pulses match the cycling of sump pumps in homes with foundation drains connected to the sanitary lateral.
Streets where sump pumps discharge to the surface show no pulses and lower storm peaks.
Dry weather flow is the same in both street types.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pulses are lift station cycles upstream
Connected sump pumps deliver foundation drainage to the sanitary sewer in pulses, and surface discharging streets prove the connection is the difference
Residents shower in ten minute rotations during storms
The flow meter creates pulses in wet weather

inference.explanation: Pulses match sump cycling, appear only where pumps connect to the sanitary system, and vanish where pumps discharge to surface, at equal dry flow. No lift station serves the street. The connection, not the pump itself, is the program target.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Street by street sump connection survey with storm hydrographs for connected and surface discharge streets
Lift station run records for the area
Flow meter diagnostic reports

nextClue.explanation: The paired street comparison quantifies what disconnection can remove, which sizes the program honestly.

clueText.nc-a: Connected streets peak about twice as high as surface streets in the same storms, at equal home counts.
clueText.nc-b: No lift station discharges into these gravity streets.
clueText.nc-c: Diagnostics are clean, and meters do not know which streets connect sumps.

tasks.prompt: Roof leader disconnection is done on half a street, and the result guides the rest.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Before work, the street sewer peaked at 60 L/s in a standard storm.
After disconnecting roof leaders on the upstream half of the street, the same size storm peaks at 42 L/s.
The downstream half, not yet disconnected, shows the same fast response timing as before.
Night flow is unchanged by the disconnections.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Disconnection also reduced infiltration in the street
The peak cut matches the disconnected share, and the remaining fast response sits in the still connected half, supporting completion of the street
The lower peak is due to a smaller storm
Night flow should have fallen if disconnection worked

inference.explanation: Storms are matched, the peak fell in proportion to the disconnected share, and the fast response that remains maps to the connected half. Night flow is an infiltration measure, so its stability confirms disconnection removed inflow only, exactly as expected.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Before and after hydrographs with the disconnection map by address
Night flow records alone
Resident feedback forms

nextClue.explanation: Hydrographs with the address map attribute the remaining peak to the unfinished half, street by street.

clueText.nc-a: The residual fast peak timing matches flow travel from the connected downstream half only.
clueText.nc-b: Night flow was never the target of disconnection, so it cannot judge it.
clueText.nc-c: Feedback does not measure storm peaks.

tasks.prompt: A cross connection between storm and sanitary sewers is confirmed by two methods.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Dye placed in a storm manhole appears in the sanitary manhole below within minutes.
Sanitary flow rises within minutes of rain starting, even after roof leader disconnections are complete.
CCTV from the sanitary side shows a direct connecting pipe between the two systems at a shared manhole wall.
Dry weather sanitary flow is normal, with no dye transfer in dry tests.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roof leaders that were missed explain the fast response
A direct storm to sanitary connection is transferring stormwater, proven by dye timing and the connecting pipe on camera
The dye leaked through the manhole benching cracks
Groundwater carries the dye between the systems

inference.explanation: Dye moves in minutes, a physical connecting pipe is on camera, and transfer happens only when the storm side carries water. Benching cracks or groundwater cannot move dye in minutes in a directed stream, and disconnections are already complete.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: CCTV still of the connecting pipe with the dye test timing record
Roof leader reinspection list
Groundwater level records

nextClue.explanation: The camera image of the pipe plus the timed dye transfer is conclusive evidence for a repair order.

clueText.nc-a: The still shows an open 200 mm connection through the shared wall, and dye transit takes under five minutes in rain.
clueText.nc-b: Reinspection finds no missed roof leaders on the contributing streets.
clueText.nc-c: Groundwater moves far too slowly for a five minute transfer.

tasks.prompt: Foundation drain flow keeps one lateral running clear and full in dry weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: The lateral runs with clear water at a steady rate through a two week dry period.
The home sump pit fills steadily from its foundation drains and its pump discharges to the lateral.
Water in the lateral tests as low in sewage indicators and matches groundwater in temperature.
Neighbours laterals run at normal sewage rates with dry sump pits.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The home has a leaking water service flooding its lateral
Foundation drainage collected by the sump is being pumped to the sanitary lateral, adding clear groundwater full time
The lateral is taking water from the main sewer
The home uses far more water than its neighbours

inference.explanation: The water is clear, groundwater like, steady in dry weather, and the sump fills from foundation drains with its discharge to the lateral. A water service leak would show in the home water meter and would not fill the sump pit from the drains. Flow direction from main to lateral contradicts levels and the pump record.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Sump pump discharge tracing and a water meter check for the home
Main sewer depth records
Neighbour water bills

nextClue.explanation: Tracing the sump discharge and ruling out a service leak separates the two clear water sources.

clueText.nc-a: The pump discharge pipe runs directly to the lateral, and the home meter shows no leak flow when fixtures are off.
clueText.nc-b: Main depth is below the lateral outlet, so the main cannot fill it.
clueText.nc-c: Bills do not locate where sump water is discharged.

tasks.prompt: A private lateral offset at the property line splits responsibility for a recurring blockage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Blockages recur at a fixed point 0.5 m on the municipal side of the property line.
Camera from the main shows an offset joint at that point with roots entering.
The private portion of the lateral, from the home to the line, is new plastic and defect free.
Two homes sharing the municipal portion beyond the line both experience the backups.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Each home is responsible for its own plumbing faults
The defect sits in the shared municipal portion at the offset joint, so the repair belongs to the municipal side program
The new plastic laterals are causing the blockages
Roots at the joint are the homeowners trees, so location does not matter

inference.explanation: The defect is located by camera on the municipal side of the line, the private portions are verified sound, and both homes sharing that municipal length are affected. Responsibility follows the located defect, not the species of tree feeding the roots.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Lateral camera log with distances tied to the surveyed property line, for both homes
Tree ownership records for the street
Home plumbing inspection reports

nextClue.explanation: Distance tied camera evidence against the surveyed line is what assigns the repair correctly.

clueText.nc-a: Both laterals meet the offset joint on the municipal side, and the joint is the only defect in either run.
clueText.nc-b: Tree ownership does not move the property line or the joint.
clueText.nc-c: Home plumbing is verified clear by the same camera runs.

tasks.prompt: An area drain in a sunken driveway is found connected to the sanitary sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: The driveway drain grate takes the full runoff of a paved court in storms.
Dye poured at the grate appears in the sanitary manhole within minutes during a hose test.
The storm sewer in the street runs at low level during the same test.
Sanitary flow spikes from this one property match rainfall intensity closely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The drain is connected to the storm sewer as designed
The driveway drain is cross connected to the sanitary sewer and delivers the court runoff as direct inflow
The dye reached the sanitary sewer through the soil
The flow spikes come from the home indoor water use in storms

inference.explanation: Dye arrives in minutes by hose test, the storm sewer stays low, and sanitary spikes track rainfall from this property. Soil cannot pass dye in minutes, and indoor use does not track rainfall intensity.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Hose test record with dye timing and both manhole observations
Original subdivision design drawings alone
Home water use records

nextClue.explanation: The controlled hose test removes weather guesswork and proves the connection path directly.

clueText.nc-a: Dye appears in the sanitary manhole in three minutes while the storm manhole stays clear through the whole test.
clueText.nc-b: Drawings show intent, the test shows the as built connection.
clueText.nc-c: Indoor use does not rise and fall with a hose test.

tasks.prompt: A rental property shows repeated lateral blockages that stop when the tenant changes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Blockages are wipes and hygiene products, always in the lateral, never in the main.
The main and the other laterals on the street stay clear through the same period.
After the tenant leaves, the same lateral runs two years with no blockage under a new tenant.
The lateral itself is sound on camera with good grade and no roots or offsets.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lateral has an intermittent structural fault
The blockages came from what the former tenant flushed, because the sound lateral serves a new tenant cleanly for two years
The main is undersized for the street
Wipes dissolve in two years, which explains the clear period

inference.explanation: The lateral is structurally sound, the material is flushable misuse products, the main and neighbours are clear, and the same pipe performs perfectly under different use. Structure cannot switch with tenancy, behaviour can.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Lateral camera report with blockage material records and the two year clear history
Main capacity calculations
Wipe product packaging claims

nextClue.explanation: The sound camera report plus the behaviour change history closes the case without digging.

clueText.nc-a: The camera shows a clean, sound lateral, and every blockage in the record predates the tenant change.
clueText.nc-b: Main capacity is irrelevant to blockages confined to one lateral.
clueText.nc-c: Packaging claims do not change what was recovered from the lateral.

tasks.prompt: A private side inflow hunt uses building by building flow isolation at night and in storms.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario private side investigation. Dye, smoke and inspection results are as stated.

evidence.label: Temporary plugs isolate one building at a time at its lateral during a storm.
Plugging the arena building drops street storm flow by 35 percent, plugging homes drops it by 2 to 3 percent each.
The arena has a large roof drained by internal leaders found connected to the sanitary lateral.
Dry weather flow contributions from all buildings are similar per occupant.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Homes collectively are the main storm source and the arena is minor
The arena roof leaders dominate the street storm inflow, so one building correction removes about a third of the peak
The plugs themselves create the flow drops by storing water
Dry weather similarity means storm contributions are also similar

inference.explanation: Isolation during the storm measures each building directly. The arena alone accounts for 35 percent and has the large connected roof to explain it, while homes contribute a few percent each. Plugs store water briefly but cannot create a sustained one building share difference.

nextClue.prompt: Which record or check best tests this explanation?

options.label: Isolation test log with street flow during each plug period and the arena roof drainage plan
Dry weather flow contributions alone
Building occupant counts

nextClue.explanation: The isolation log is the measurement that ranks sources by evidence instead of by assumption.

clueText.nc-a: Street flow falls by a third only while the arena is plugged, and recovers when it is released.
clueText.nc-b: Dry weather equality is exactly why storm isolation was needed.
clueText.nc-c: Occupant counts do not describe roof drainage connections.
